screens.prompt: In B7, look up the lead time of the first Northwind supplier in A1:C6, using the partial name in A7 with a wildcard.

hints.syntax: =VLOOKUP(A7&"*",A1:C6,3,FALSE): the star turns the partial name into a pattern.
hints.func-vlookup: INDEX and MATCH could answer too, but the point here is what a wildcard does inside VLOOKUP's first argument.
hints.match-type: FALSE as the fourth argument. Approximate match sorts text and never reads the pattern, so a miss could pass as a hit.
hints.require-ref: Build the pattern from A7. A typed "Northwind*" is right today and dead tomorrow.
hints.value: That is the country. Supplier is 1, country 2, lead time 3, so the third argument is 3.
hints.error: #N/A means the pattern found no supplier: check the star. #REF! means the column number passed column C; #VALUE! means the column slot holds a word.

reject.why: two arguments is not a VLOOKUP; the column to read is missing
no fourth argument means approximate match, which never reads the pattern
approximate match compares text in sort order instead of matching the pattern
the bare word Northwind is not in the list, so exact match stops with #N/A
the pattern is typed in, so the answer never follows A7
column 2 holds the country, so this returns Ireland rather than a lead time
the column argument is a word, so there is no column to count to and the formula stops with #VALUE!
a fourth column does not exist, so the formula stops with #REF!
? stands for exactly one character, and Northwind plus one character is not a supplier
right answer, but the exercise is about VLOOKUP reading the wildcard

docs.explain:
A wildcard turns the lookup value into a pattern. A7 holds Northwind, so A7&"*" asks for the first supplier whose name starts with it. Air sits in row 4, and column 3 of A1:C6 gives its lead time, 7 days.

Without the star the lookup value is the bare word Northwind, which no cell holds, so exact match stops at #N/A. Three suppliers begin with Northwind, and the first in table order wins: Air at 7 days, and Rail's 19 never comes up.

FALSE is still required. Approximate match compares text in sort order and never reads the pattern. A longer prefix such as Northwind R narrows the field when the order matters.

errors.text: The pattern matched no supplier, usually because the star is missing or the prefix is wrong.
The column number is a word such as lead, which cannot be counted to.
The column number runs past column C, the last one in A1:C6.

docs.atWork: A purchase ledger where supplier names arrive abbreviated and only the first few letters can be trusted.
docs.outcome: Match a name you half know, and keep the pattern in a cell so it can change.

seo.title: VLOOKUP wildcard: match a partial name
seo.description: A7&"*" turns a partial name into a pattern, and VLOOKUP returns the first supplier that starts with it: Northwind Air at 7 days, not Rail at 19.
